⋈.justification: The sequential composition of Th1 through Th4, linking the possibility of a God-like being to its necessary existence.

⊙.justification: The identity where the act of proving (donor) and the state of being proven (acceptor) are unified; the God-like individual bears its own essence.

∈.justification: The fork separating the branch where a God-like being is merely possible (Th2) from the branch where it is necessary (Th4), driven by the S5 frame properties.

∋.justification: The reconstitution of the possibility and necessity arms into a single verdict where ◇□∃x G(x) lifts to □∃x G(x) via symmetry and transitivity.

⊞.justification: The paradice where the God-like individual holds all positive properties simultaneously, including necessary existence, maintaining the contradiction of finite reason and infinite bulk.

⊡.justification: The permanent record that the five axioms are satisfiable in a model with one world and one individual, fixing the proof against empirical perturbation.

Fuse the possibility and necessity arms into a single verdict of necessary existence (□∃x G(x)).
Hold the dialetheic state where the God-like individual simultaneously embodies all positive properties and necessary existence.
Establish the self-referential identity where the proof and the proven are one.

Chain the modal collapse theorem to show that everything true is necessarily true.
Anchor the system in the modal collapse state where surface and interior are one register.
